msrathaus.name: Historic Town Hall
msrathaus.slogan: The gabled hall where Europe signed away thirty years of war.
msrathaus.line: The Peace of Westphalia treaties of 24 October 1648 ended the Thirty Years' War, a conflict that killed an estimated 4.5 to 8 million people.

msdom.name: St. Paul's Cathedral
msdom.slogan: A 109-metre Gothic giant with a clock that still tells the planets.
msdom.line: Its astronomical clock was installed between 1540 and 1542, replacing one the Anabaptists destroyed in 1534.

mslamberti.name: St. Lamberti Church
mslamberti.slogan: Three iron cages and a horn that sounds over the rooftops.
mslamberti.line: Since 1379 a tower watchman has blown a horn from the tower every half-hour from 9 p.m. to midnight.

msnordkirchen.name: Nordkirchen Palace
msnordkirchen.slogan: Westphalia's Versailles, moated and mirrored in its own pond.
msnordkirchen.line: The largest moated palace in Westphalia was built mostly between 1703 and 1734, set in a park of about 170 hectares.

msvischering.name: Burg Vischering
msvischering.slogan: A horseshoe of brick afloat on a moat fed by the Stever.
msvischering.line: Burned down in 1521, the castle was rebuilt on its original foundations and today houses the Münsterlandmuseum.
